title: Lipid metabolism-associated genes serve as potential predictive biomarkers in neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy combined with immunotherapy in rectal cancer.
authors: Peng, Qiliang; Tao, Jialong; Xu, Yingjie; Shen, Yi; Wang, Yong; Jiao, Yang; Mao, Yiheng; Zhu, Yaqun; Liu, Yulong; Tian, Ye
one_liner_zh: 该研究关注直肠癌脂代谢基因作为新辅助放化疗联合免疫治疗预测标志物，虽涉及转录因子SREBF2但仅作表达与预后关联分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate the potential role of lipid metabolism-associated genes (LMAGs) in neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) and immunotherapy for rectal cancer. METHODS: Differential LMAGs were characterized and functional enrichment analysis was performed. Multiple machine learning algorithms were combined to explore candidate LMAGs. ROC analysis was performed to evaluate the predicting accuracy of candidate LMAGs. The expression patterns, prognostic value, genetic alterations, and immune cell infiltration of the top-ranked LMAGs were investigated. RESULTS: We identified 45 LMAGs that were differentially expressed in tumor samples of nCRT responders and non-responders. These LMAGs were closely associated with lipid metabolism-related biological processes and pathways. ROC analysis revealed that the SREBF2 gene, an important transcription factor in regulating lipid metabolism, was the highest predictor of nCRT in rectal cancer. SREBF2 was highly expressed in rectal cancer tissues and high expression of SREBF2 was associated with favorable prognosis. Multivariate analysis showed that SREBF2 was an independent prognostic factor, and we integrated it with other clinical factors to establish an effective prognostic nomogram. SREBF2 also played a synergistic role with its co-expressed genes in the prognostic process of rectal cancer. Furthermore, SREBF2 was demonstrated to be closely associated with multiple immune infiltrating cells, and immunotherapy-related genes and may be used to predict the response to immunotherapy. CONCLUSION: Our study suggests that LMAGs may serve as promising biomarkers in nCRT combined with immunotherapy for rectal cancer. However, large-scale clinical trials and biological experiments are necessary to demonstrate the efficacy and underlying mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究旨在探讨脂质代谢相关基因（LMAGs）在直肠癌新辅助放化疗（nCRT）及免疫治疗中的潜在作用。方法：对差异表达的LMAGs进行表征，并进行功能富集分析。结合多种机器学习算法探索候选LMAGs。采用ROC分析评估候选LMAGs的预测准确性。研究了排名靠前的LMAGs的表达模式、预后价值、遗传改变及免疫细胞浸润情况。结果：我们在nCRT应答者与非应答者的肿瘤样本中鉴定出45个差异表达的LMAGs。这些LMAGs与脂质代谢相关的生物学过程和通路密切相关。ROC分析显示，SREBF2基因（调控脂质代谢的重要转录因子）是直肠癌nCRT的最高预测因子。SREBF2在直肠癌组织中高表达，且其高表达与良好预后相关。多变量分析表明，SREBF2是独立预后因素，我们将其与其他临床因素整合，建立了一个有效的预后列线图。SREBF2还与其共表达基因在直肠癌预后过程中发挥协同作用。此外，SREBF2被证明与多种免疫浸润细胞及免疫治疗相关基因密切相关，并可能用于预测免疫治疗反应。结论：我们的研究表明，LMAGs可能作为直肠癌nCRT联合免疫治疗的有前景的生物标志物。然而，需要大规模临床试验和生物学实验来验证其疗效及潜在机制。
